scope_note: Structured, analysis-oriented representation of Chrome Web Store Program Policies. Requirements are paraphrased for machine use; use source_url for the canonical policy text.

clauses.requirement: Developers must comply with Chrome Web Store Developer Program Policies and the Developer Agreement.
clauses.analysis_notes: Use as general context; do not cite alone as a breach without a more specific clause.

clauses.requirement: Policies apply to the entire product experience, including extension code, marketing materials, user-generated content, ads, and landing pages unless stated otherwise.
clauses.analysis_notes: Useful when behavior occurs outside packaged source code, such as landing pages or ads.

clauses.requirement: Developers should review Chrome Web Store policies and ensure extension compliance.
clauses.analysis_notes: Usually not directly testable from code.

clauses.requirement: Extensions should provide useful or unique value to users.
clauses.analysis_notes: Needs product/listing context; code alone rarely proves this.

clauses.requirement: Developers must not scam the system, mislead users, circumvent enforcement, copy other developers' work, or manipulate ratings/reviews.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires evidence of manipulation or deceptive behavior.

clauses.requirement: Developers must follow strict rules for collecting, using, and disclosing user data and must obtain consent for data collection or use.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map to specific privacy clauses before alleging a breach.

clauses.requirement: Extension metadata and developer dashboard information, including privacy certifications and item category, must be accurate and current.
Extensions should be tested for crashes, broken features, and bugs before submission.
clauses.analysis_notes: Usually outside static reverse engineering unless broken code paths are evident.

clauses.requirement: Developer contact information should be correct so Chrome Web Store can reach the publisher.
The single purpose field should describe the extension's primary functionality in detail.
clauses.analysis_notes: Compare observed workflows to listing/single-purpose text when available.

clauses.requirement: Developers should provide meaningful customer support.
Developers are responsible for keeping up with policy changes.
Content with nudity, graphic sex acts, sexually explicit material, or traffic to commercial pornography is not allowed.
Content promoting incest, bestiality, necrophilia, or non-consensual sexual acts is not allowed.
Child sexual abuse material is zero-tolerance and leads to reporting and account deletion.
Non-sexual nudity may be allowed but may affect product visibility.
clauses.analysis_notes: Visibility concern, not automatically a breach.

clauses.requirement: Products unsuitable for all ages should be marked mature in the Developer Dashboard.
Extensions must not transmit viruses, worms, defects, Trojan horses, malware, or destructive products.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires strong evidence of malicious payload or destructive behavior.

clauses.requirement: Extensions must not harm or interfere with Google or third-party networks, servers, or infrastructure.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires evidence of harmful traffic or interference.

clauses.requirement: Spyware, malicious scripts, and phishing scams are prohibited.
clauses.analysis_notes: Useful for covert data capture, credential phishing, or harmful script injection.

clauses.requirement: Extensions must not facilitate unauthorized access to website content, such as bypassing paywalls or login restrictions.
Extensions must not enable unauthorized access, download, or streaming of copyrighted content or media.
Cryptocurrency mining is not allowed.
clauses.analysis_notes: Look for mining pools, WebAssembly miners, or CPU mining behavior.

clauses.requirement: Products must not contain gratuitous violence or threaten, harass, or bully users.
Products must not advocate against or incite hatred toward protected or marginalized groups.
Products must not recruit, fundraise, or promote violence on behalf of extremist groups.
Generally hateful content may affect product visibility even if not covered by explicit hate-speech removal rules.
Extensions must not engage in or promote unlawful or dangerous activities.
Real-money gambling facilitation or promotion is not allowed; simulated gambling must clearly state no real money is involved.
Extensions must not facilitate sale of regulated goods or services such as pharmaceuticals, alcohol, tobacco, fireworks, weapons, gambling, or health/medical devices.
If a product handles user data, it must provide an accurate and up-to-date privacy policy.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires evidence that user data is handled and policy availability/status.

clauses.requirement: The privacy policy and in-product disclosures must disclose how user data is collected, used, and shared.
clauses.analysis_notes: Use observed_privacy_data plus external privacy policy comparison.

clauses.requirement: The privacy policy and in-product disclosures must disclose all parties that receive shared user data.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map network endpoints and recipients to policy disclosures.

clauses.requirement: A privacy policy link must be provided in the Chrome Web Store Developer Dashboard field.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires Chrome Web Store extraction; code alone cannot prove.

clauses.requirement: Chrome Web Store rules are minimum user data privacy requirements and products must also comply with applicable law.
clauses.analysis_notes: Use as context, not standalone breach evidence.

clauses.requirement: Use of user data must be limited to the practices disclosed.
Collection and use of web browsing activity is prohibited except when required for a prominently disclosed user-facing feature in the store page and UI.
clauses.analysis_notes: High-value clause for extensions with broad host access or URL transmission.

clauses.requirement: Limited Use requirements apply to raw, aggregated, anonymized, de-identified, derived, scraped, and automatically gathered user data.
clauses.analysis_notes: Prevents dismissing derived telemetry as out of scope.

clauses.requirement: User data use must be limited to providing or improving the product's single purpose.
clauses.analysis_notes: Compare data uses to product purpose and disclosures.

clauses.requirement: Transfer of user data to third parties is allowed only when necessary to provide or improve the single purpose.
clauses.analysis_notes: Needs necessity argument and disclosure context.

clauses.requirement: Transfer of user data to third parties may be allowed to comply with applicable laws.
Transfer of user data may be allowed to protect against malware, spam, phishing, fraud, or abuse.
Transfer of user data may be allowed as part of merger, acquisition, or asset sale after explicit prior user consent.
Humans must not read user data unless the user gives explicit consent to read specific data.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires policy/backend/support process evidence; code may show data sent to servers.

clauses.requirement: Human access may be allowed when data is aggregated and anonymized for internal operations under applicable privacy law.
Human access may be allowed when necessary for security purposes such as investigating abuse.
Human access may be allowed to comply with applicable laws.
Transferring, using, or selling user data for personalized advertising is prohibited.
clauses.analysis_notes: Needs ad/personalization behavior and data-transfer evidence.

clauses.requirement: Transferring or selling user data to advertising platforms, data brokers, or information resellers is prohibited.
Transferring, using, or selling user data for credit-worthiness or lending purposes is prohibited.
clauses.analysis_notes: Rare in extension source; requires strong evidence.

clauses.requirement: A website belonging to the extension must affirm that Google API data use adheres to Chrome Web Store User Data Policy, including Limited Use.
clauses.analysis_notes: Relevant when OAuth/Google APIs are present; requires website/policy verification.

clauses.requirement: Extensions must request the narrowest permissions necessary; when multiple permissions could implement a feature, choose the least access. Do not future-proof with unused broad permissions.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map manifest permissions to observed workflows and user-facing purpose.

clauses.requirement: Developers must transparently disclose collection, use, and sharing of user data, including information provided by or collected about the user or their Chrome/product use.
clauses.analysis_notes: Needs declared privacy and external policy comparison.

clauses.requirement: If user data handling is not closely related to prominently described functionality, the product must prominently disclose what data is collected and how it is used before installation.
clauses.analysis_notes: Compare observed behavior to store listing/UI purpose.

clauses.requirement: If non-core user data is handled, the product must obtain affirmative and informed user consent before installation.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires UI/store consent evidence; code alone often insufficient.

clauses.requirement: Products associated with exploitable security vulnerabilities may be removed and require remediation.
clauses.analysis_notes: Use for concrete vulnerability findings, not generic risk.

clauses.requirement: Products collecting user data must handle it securely, including transmission using modern cryptography.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map user data transfers to HTTPS/crypto evidence.

clauses.requirement: Financial or payment information must not be publicly disclosed.
Authentication information must be kept secure and must not be publicly disclosed.
clauses.analysis_notes: High-value clause for auth tokens, cookies, and credential handling.

clauses.requirement: Products must not impersonate or falsely claim authorization, endorsement, or production by another company or organization.
Products and user experience must not mimic operating system or browser functionality or warnings.
clauses.analysis_notes: Relevant to overlays, notifications, fake security UI.

clauses.requirement: Developers must not divert users or link to sites that mimic or pass themselves off as the Chrome Web Store.
Metadata must not misrepresent extension or developer status or performance.
Products must not infringe intellectual property rights.
Potential intellectual property infringement may affect product visibility.
Extensions must be marketed responsibly; promised functionality must be clear and user interaction outcomes must match reasonable expectations.
Advertisements or marketing before installation must not be confusing or deceptive and must make product features clear.
Interactive elements before installation must not mislead users; calls to action must state that an extension will be installed.
Chrome Web Store product listing windows must not be adjusted to hide or withhold extension metadata.
Installation flows must not bundle other extensions or offers.
Users must not be required to take unrelated actions to access advertised functionality.
Sensitive personal information collected for sales, including payment data, must be securely collected, stored, and transmitted under applicable rules.
Products or services sold through the extension must be clearly and honestly described, including terms, refunds, and returns.
If payment is required for basic functionality, that must be clear before installation.
The seller must be clearly identified as the developer, not Google.
Payment processing must not involve prohibited transactions or prohibited goods or services.
Products must not deceive or mislead users through content, title, description, or screenshots.
Changes to device settings must be made with user knowledge and consent and must be easily reversible.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map to settings APIs and UI consent.

clauses.requirement: Products must not misrepresent functionality or include non-obvious functionality unrelated to the primary purpose.
clauses.analysis_notes: Important for hidden tracking, affiliate, ads, or extra workflows.

clauses.requirement: Products must not claim impossible functionality.
Privacy, security, or anti-virus extensions must provide discernible monitoring or protection.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires product category/listing and code behavior.

clauses.requirement: Ads are part of the product for policy review and must comply with content policies.
clauses.analysis_notes: Use as context for ad workflows.

clauses.requirement: Ads inconsistent with the product content rating violate developer terms.
AdSense may not be used to serve ads in products.
Ads must be presented in context or clearly state which product they are bundled with.
Ads must be easily removable through settings or uninstalling the product.
Ads must not simulate or impersonate system notifications or warnings.
Users must not be forced to click ads or submit personal information for advertising to fully use the product.
Ads shown alongside third-party websites must be clearly disclosed to the user.
Ads shown alongside third-party websites must clearly attribute the ad source.
Ads must not interfere with native ads or functionality of the third-party website.
Ads must not mimic or impersonate native ads or content on third-party websites.
Affiliate programs must be prominently described in the Chrome Web Store page, user interface, and before installation.

Affiliate links, codes, or cookies may be included only with direct and transparent user benefit related to core functionality; injecting affiliate links without user action and benefit is not permitted.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map URL/cookie modifications to user action and benefit.

clauses.requirement: Affiliate links must not be inserted when no discount, cashback, or donation is provided.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires product behavior and benefit evidence.

clauses.requirement: Extensions must not continuously inject affiliate links in the background without related user action.
clauses.analysis_notes: High-value clause for background shopping modifications.

clauses.requirement: Related user action is required before each affiliate code, link, or cookie is included.
Updating shopping-related cookies without user knowledge while browsing shopping sites is a common violation.
clauses.analysis_notes: Relevant to cookies permission and shopping domains.

clauses.requirement: Appending or replacing affiliate codes in URLs without explicit user knowledge and related action is a common violation.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map navigation/redirect code to user action.

clauses.requirement: Applying or replacing affiliate promo codes without explicit user knowledge and related action is a common violation.

Certain products may be restricted from featuring even without explicit policy violation, including VPNs, video downloaders, anti-virus tools, bots, cryptocurrency, non-production builds, prohibited products, gambling content, and products from questionable developer reputations.
Developers and affiliates must not submit multiple extensions with duplicate experiences or functionality.
Developers must not manipulate placement, ratings, reviews, or install counts through illegitimate means.
Extensions must not abuse notifications by sending spam, ads, promotions, phishing attempts, or unwanted messages that harm browsing experience.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map notifications API usage to purpose/triggers.

clauses.requirement: Extensions must not send messages on behalf of the user without allowing the user to confirm content and recipients.
Extensions must comply with Google's Webmaster Quality Guidelines.
An extension must have a single narrow purpose and must not require users to accept bundled unrelated functionality.
clauses.analysis_notes: Compare observed workflows to primary purpose/listing.

clauses.requirement: Combining product ratings/reviews functionality with ad injection is a common single-purpose violation example.
Toolbars with broad arrays of functionality or entry points are better as separate extensions.
Combining email notifier functionality with a news aggregator is a common unrelated-functionality example.
New Tab Page extensions that alter search experience and do not respect existing search settings are a common violation example.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map to chrome_settings_overrides, search changes, or new tab behavior.

clauses.requirement: Extensions should enhance the browsing task while causing minimal distractions, especially when using persistent UI.
Side panel extensions that hijack browsing or search experience are common quality violations.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map side panel behavior to user control.

clauses.requirement: Extensions whose primary purpose is serving ads are common quality violations.
Products with blank description fields or missing icons/screenshots will be rejected.
Listing information must be current, accurate, comprehensive, properly formatted, descriptive, and appropriate.
Privacy fields must be accurate and current; contradictions with privacy policy or extension behavior may lead to removal.
clauses.analysis_notes: Core clause for prompt3-5 comparison outputs.

clauses.requirement: Keyword spam, including irrelevant/excessive keywords or unnatural repetition, is not allowed.
Lists of sites, brands, or keywords without substantial added value are keyword-spam examples.
Lists of regional locations are keyword-spam examples.
Unnatural repetition of the same keyword more than five times is a keyword-spam example.
Unattributed or anonymous user testimonials in product descriptions are not allowed.
Extensions must not have the sole purpose of installing or launching another app, theme, webpage, or extension.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map workflows to actual extension functionality.

clauses.requirement: Extensions with broken functionality, dead sites, or non-functioning features are not allowed.
Extensions must provide basic functionality and utility that adds value to the Chrome Web Store catalog.
Extensions with no functionality or utility are common minimum-functionality violations.
clauses.analysis_notes: Use only when code/workflows show no useful function.

clauses.requirement: Extensions whose functionality is not directly provided by the extension, such as link-only file converters, are common violations.
Clickbait template extensions with negligible utility are common minimum-functionality violations.
Packaged apps should use platform capabilities and not merely wrap an existing website or launch a webpage.
clauses.analysis_notes: Applies only to Chrome Apps, not normal extensions.

clauses.requirement: Packaged apps should detect offline state and clearly message it to users.
Packaged apps should recover automatically from loss of internet connectivity.
Packaged and hosted apps should not require a local executable other than Chrome runtime.
clauses.analysis_notes: Applies only to Chrome Apps; native messaging in extensions needs separate policy context.

clauses.requirement: Packaged and hosted apps should not provide a WebView of a website not owned or administered by the developer.
Packaged and hosted apps should not download or execute scripts dynamically outside a sandboxed environment.
clauses.analysis_notes: Applies to Chrome Apps; MV3 has separate remote-logic clauses.

clauses.requirement: Packaged and hosted apps should not misuse notifications for spam, ads, promotions, phishing, or unwanted messages.
clauses.analysis_notes: Applies only to Chrome Apps; similar extension spam clause exists.

clauses.requirement: Developers must not obfuscate code or conceal extension functionality; minification is allowed.
clauses.analysis_notes: Differentiate allowed minification from functionality concealment.

clauses.requirement: Allowed minification includes removing whitespace, newlines, comments, and block delimiters.
clauses.analysis_notes: Do not treat minification alone as obfuscation.

clauses.requirement: Allowed minification includes shortening variable and function names.
clauses.analysis_notes: Do not treat short names alone as obfuscation.

clauses.requirement: Allowed minification includes collapsing files together.
clauses.analysis_notes: Bundling alone is not a breach.

clauses.requirement: Extensions must use existing Chrome APIs for their designated use case when such APIs exist; alternate methods may violate policy.
Manifest V3 extension functionality must be easily discernible from submitted code; external resources must not contain logic unless exempt.
clauses.analysis_notes: Core clause for remote logic/config analysis.

clauses.requirement: Including script tags that point to resources outside the extension package is a common MV3 violation.
clauses.analysis_notes: Map CSP, HTML, DOM script creation, and web_accessible resources.

clauses.requirement: Using eval or similar mechanisms to execute strings fetched from remote sources is a common MV3 violation.
clauses.analysis_notes: Requires remote source plus execution sink.

clauses.requirement: Building an interpreter to run complex commands fetched from remote sources can violate MV3 remote logic rules.
clauses.analysis_notes: Remote config can be allowed if it does not contain executable logic.

clauses.requirement: Remote execution is allowed only through documented APIs that explicitly permit it and only for the documented purpose.
clauses.analysis_notes: Check whether remote logic uses permitted APIs and purpose.

clauses.requirement: Debugger API is a permitted API for specific remote-execution cases when used within documented purpose.
clauses.analysis_notes: Do not treat debugger use as automatically allowed; purpose matters.

clauses.requirement: User Scripts API is a permitted API for specific remote-execution cases when used within documented purpose.
Remote code in isolated contexts such as iframes or sandboxed pages may be exempt from remote-code restrictions, but functionality must remain determinable and user-data policies still apply.
clauses.analysis_notes: Do not ignore privacy implications of sandboxed/iframe remote content.

clauses.requirement: Syncing user account data with a remote server is an allowed remote communication purpose.
clauses.analysis_notes: Allowed purpose, still subject to privacy/security policies.

clauses.requirement: Fetching remote configuration for A/B testing or feature enablement is allowed when functionality logic remains inside the extension package.
clauses.analysis_notes: Important mitigation for remote_config risks; distinguish data config from logic.

clauses.requirement: Fetching remote resources that are not used to evaluate logic, such as images, is allowed.
clauses.analysis_notes: Allowed purpose unless privacy/security issue exists.

clauses.requirement: Server-side operations with data, such as private-key encryption operations, may be allowed.
clauses.analysis_notes: Allowed purpose, still subject to data handling and disclosure.

clauses.requirement: If Chrome Web Store reviewers cannot determine full extension functionality, the submission may be rejected or removed.
clauses.analysis_notes: Use for strong uncertainty around concealed or remote-driven behavior.

clauses.requirement: Developer accounts must use 2-Step Verification before publishing or updating extensions.
Attempting to circumvent limitations or enforcement can terminate developer accounts and related accounts.
Removed products receive email notification with further instructions when applicable.
Publisher accounts should be able to receive external emails and avoid spam filtering for timely communications.
Removals are permanent unless a revision fixes the issue; enforcement is global by default unless territory-restricted.
Developers may appeal a violation decision once; no further appeals are accepted for the same violation after decision.
Frivolous appeals or misuse of appeals may result in further action.
Serious or repeated violations can suspend developer accounts, related accounts, Chrome Web Store access, and in extreme cases related Google services.
Repeated intellectual property infringement can result in account termination.
